member.name: M:Ranks.Contract.IRanksApi.RegisterMenuEntry(System.String,Ranks.Contract.RanksMenuEntry)
member.summary: Adds one line to core's menu, under the section the entry names.
member.remarks:
Call from the handshake, after core is ready. Entries are keyed on (, Section, Label), so re-registering the same row after a config reload replaces it rather than doubling it.
Core never names a module type: it holds the delegate and a string, both declared here. That is also why is not optional — an entry outliving its module is a delegate into an unloaded assembly.

member.summary: Drops every entry a module registered. Idempotent.

member.name: M:Ranks.Contract.IRanksApi.SetDisplayOverride(SwiftlyS2.Shared.Players.IPlayer,Ranks.Contract.RanksDisplayOverride)
member.summary: Overlays what the scoreboard shows for one player, leaving stored points alone.
member.remarks:
Applies immediately. Every display surface core owns — the rank icon, the mode it is drawn in, the clan tag and the synced score — is resolved from the overlay, so a module never has to write those fields itself and never fights core for the tag (FR-API-02).
Session-scoped: dropped when the player disconnects, never persisted. A module that wants it to survive a reconnect re-applies it from PlayerDataLoaded.

member.name: T:Ranks.Contract.IRanksKillArbiter
member.summary: Consulted by core before it awards a kill (FR-API-11).
member.remarks:
Core asks *before* awarding rather than letting a module react afterwards, which is the only ordering under which suppression is expressible: a module hooking player_death itself cannot stop core, and plugin order is not guaranteed.
Runs on the game thread inside core's award path. Returning fast matters, and touching the database here does not.

member.name: T:Ranks.Contract.RanksMenuEntry
member.summary: One line a module contributes to core's menu.

remarks.para: The module hands over a factory, not rows: core calls when the player opens the parent and nests whatever comes back, so the module owns its own layout, paging and colours. A menu with no parent of its own is adopted by the entry that opened it, which is what makes the player's back key return to core's menu rather than close everything.
runs on the game thread and must not block. Load inside a PagedCollectionComponent, which is built for exactly this and is how core's own leaderboard reads the database.
